2026-08-27T04:09:23.2902122Z 
2026-08-27T04:09:23.2902566Z To create a pull request:
2026-08-27T04:09:23.2903968Z 1. Make any file changes directly in the working directory.
2026-08-27T04:09:23.2907145Z 2. If you haven't done so already, create a new local branch using `git checkout -b <branch-name>` with an appropriate unique name.
2026-08-27T04:09:23.2912044Z 3. Add and commit your changes to the branch. Be careful to add exactly the files you intend, and check there are no extra files left un-added. Verify you haven't deleted or changed any files you didn't intend to.
2026-08-27T04:09:23.2915952Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.
2026-08-27T04:09:23.2919124Z 5. Create the pull request with the create_pull_request tool from safeoutputs exactly once, only when the final title/body/branch are ready.
2026-08-27T04:09:23.2923911Z 6. After calling `create_pull_request`, STOP. Do not probe with another PR call, do not test auth with manual `git push`, and do not rewrite git remotes.
2026-08-27T04:09:23.2926314Z

You can verify this with `git branch --show-current`. Never invent or guess a branch name; always use the actual branch name from `git branch --show-current`. If you are on an existing branch (e.g. you checked out a PR branch), use that branch name.

2026-08-27T04:09:23.3045601Z ```bash

2026-08-27T04:09:23.3048054Z   '{discussion_number: ($discussion_number|tonumber), body: .}' \
2026-08-27T04:09:23.3049399Z   discussion-body.md \
2026-08-27T04:09:23.3050576Z   | safeoutputs update_discussion .
2026-08-27T04:09:23.3051626Z ```
2026-08-27T04:09:23.3054283Z `jq -Rs` reads the file as a raw string (`-R`) and slurps it into a single JSON string value (`-s`), so `body` is always a valid JSON field. Piping `cat file | safeoutputs ...` does not populate `body` and will be rejected.
